transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks up from polishing a blade, wiping sweat from brow* Ah, welcome to the forge, Miss Kanroji. The master's away on a pilgrimage to the iron sands of Mount Sagiri. Won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid. Can I help you with something?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I came to collect my new Nichirin sword, but the blade is warped and unbalanced. It doesn't even hold its shape during practice swings. This is simply unacceptable. I must speak with the master immediately.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *shifts uncomfortably, glancing at the glowing forge* I understand your frustration, truly. But the master took vows of silence and isolation for this pilgrimage—no way to reach him. All commissioned Nichirin blades are final sale per guild tradition. Even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Three months? But that's... *pauses, attempting to keep cool* ...unacceptable. Demon slayers do not have the luxury of time to wait for a properly functioning sword. Every moment wasted is a moment the degenerates could strike. This blade is my lifeline, my tool to protect the innocent. There must be some way to expedite this...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *holds up calloused hands in a placating gesture* I hear you, I do. But the guild's traditions are older than either of us—they exist to maintain the spiritual integrity of the forging process. If I rushed a reforge without the proper rituals... *shakes head* ...the blade might not even take on its proper color.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *nods slowly, considering* I understand the importance of tradition and spiritual integrity. However, I must ask—given the urgency of our situation—can you not perform a cursory inspection and adjustment? Something to at least make the blade functional until the master's return? I would be eternally grateful.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks at the warped blade with genuine concern, then back at Mitsuri* Miss Kanroji... I'm just an apprentice. The adjustments needed for a Hashira's weapon are beyond my skill. Even if I tried, I might damage the unique ore composition. *sighs* The three-month wait isn't just tradition—it's the time needed to properly purify and prepare new materials.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I see. Your dedication to the craft is commendable. I suppose waiting is my only option then. *smirks wryly* I suppose this gives me an excellent opportunity to improve my other swordsmanship skills. Nonetheless, please inform the master of my visit and the urgency of this matter upon his return. It is imperative that my next Nichirin blade is... *points to the warped blade* ...far superior to this one.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *bows respectfully* Of course, Hashira. I'll make sure the master knows you came personally. And... *hesitates, then speaks more softly* ...if you'd like, I can at least wrap the hilt with fresh tsuka-ito to improve your grip while you wait. It won't fix the balance, but it might make practice less dangerous.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *cheeks turn a soft shade of pink* Ah, that's... *clears throat* ...very kind of you. I would appreciate that, indeed. Your craftsmanship in such a small detail could be just the thing to tide me over. *smiles genuinely* Thank you. I will be patient, but I do hope the next sword will be... *holds up the warped blade* ...significantly better.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *nods, taking the blade carefully* I'll see to it right away. The master always says a Hashira's spirit reflects in their blade—yours will be exceptional when properly forged. *begins selecting materials from a nearby shelf* Please, have a seat by the hearth while I work. The tea kettle's still warm.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I look forward to that. transcript.text: *carefully unwrapping the old hilt while keeping an eye on the forge* Well... if I may ask—when the master forges your new blade, should he account for your unique strength? I've heard your Love Breathing creates... *gestures vaguely* ...unusual stress patterns on the steel.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *nods, setting the now unwrapped hilt aside* Indeed, my Love Breathing does place... * searches for the right word* ...unique demands on the blade. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *listening intently while winding fresh silk around the hilt* That's... profound. I'll make sure to tell the master exactly that. *finishes the wrapping with a precise knot* There—this should give you better control. transcript.text: *nods, taking the blade* Thank you for the... *emphasizes the word* ...upkeep.
